item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q009_heme_bundle_fold_not_homology","answer":"No. SCOPe places all three groups in class f (membrane and cell-surface proteins and peptides) and the shared heme-binding four-helical-bundle fold f.21, but separates them into distinct superfamilies: transmembrane di-heme cytochromes (f.21.1), fumarate-reductase respiratory-complex transmembrane subunits (f.21.2), and respiratory nitrate-reductase gamma chains (f.21.3). A common fold records architectural similarity, not the probable common ancestry asserted at superfamily level; family-level relatedness would be stronger still. Thus heme binding and a four-helix topology do not justify merging these groups, transferring substrate or respiratory-complex functions, or selecting a member of one superfamily as a homologous template or representative for another. Cross-group homology would require independent evidence such as significant sequence/profile similarity and phylogenetic support; absent that, any cross-superfamily structural template use is fold-level analogy only.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
